newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate jumps on dollar buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate jumps on dollar buying.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate rose to a three-month high in late trade on Wednesday as banks borrowed funds to buy the dollar in foreign exchange markets, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate was quoted at 17.00-18.00 percent near the close compared with 12.00-13.00 percent in early afternoon trade, dealers said.
"Lenders were reluctant to offer funds today. They wanted to keep funds to speculate in the foreign exchange market," one dealer at a foreign bank said.
The interbank rate of 17.00-18.00 percent is the highest level since February 2 when it jumped to 25.00-28.00 percent.
Dealers expect the interbank to stay high on Thursday, unless dollar buying eases.
The baht was heavily sold for the dollar on Wednesday due to concern about the slowing economy and rumours of possible resignation of Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan, dealers said.

The baht was trading around 26.330/26.430 to the dollar late, compared with 26.000/26.050 early. Amnuay told Reuters in Tokyo he was confident in his future as Thailand's finance minister. -- Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642
